A menu of optional exercises: pick any, in any order, at your own pace.\n6\t\n7\t---\n8\t\n9\t## Front matter\n10\t### What this is\n11\tMP2plus is a **menu of 15 independent exercises** that extend the CMS you built in MP2. Pick any number, in any order, and stop whenever you like. Your points are **added to your MP2 score**, up to **+30**.\n12\t\n13\tThe menu has three groups:\n14\t- **Features** (F1–F9) come from MP2's stretch list, which MP2 introduced but did not score.\n15\t- **Process** (P1–P4) covers habits MP2 introduced but did not require, or scored only lightly.\n16\t- **Security** (S1–S2) extends two lines of `SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md` that MP2 scored only lightly.\n17\t\n18\t### The menu\n19\t| Id | Exercise | Minutes | Pts |\n20\t|---|---|---|---|\n21\t| F1 | Media uploads with alt text | 45–60 | 9 |\n22\t| F2 | Categories and tags | 40–55 | 8 |\n23\t| F3 | Revision history with rollback | 40–55 | 8 |\n24\t| F4 | Scheduled publishing | 35–50 | 7 |\n25\t| F5 | Site search | 35–50 | 7 |\n26\t| F6 | Comments with moderation | 45–60 | 9 |\n27\t| F7 | Plugin or hook system | 45–60 | 9 |\n28\t| F8 | Switchable theme | 35–50 | 7 |\n29\t| F9 | Production configuration | 40–55 | 8 |\n30\t| P1 | Pull-request workflow | 30–45 | 6 |\n31\t| P2 | `/prototype` side session | 35–50 | 7 |\n32\t| P3 | Decision record | 30–45 | 6 |\n33\t| P4 | Budget re-forecast | 30–40 | 6 |\n34\t| S1 | Direct-URL access matrix | 30–45 | 6 |\n35\t| S2 | Login hardening | 40–55 | 8 |\n36\t| | **Menu total (up to 30 count)** | | **111** |\n37\t\n38\tPick what interests you, not everything. Reaching +30 takes three or four exercises, about three hours. One or two exercises is a solid MP2plus.\n39\t\n40\t### Time and deadlines\n41\t| Milestone | What | When (Eastern, EDT) |\n42\t|---|---|---|\n43\t| **Assigned** | This manual and the rubric | **Sun Oct 11, 2026** |\n44\t| **Due** | Tag `mp2plus-final` pushed, report emailed | **Tue Oct 20, 2026, 2:40 pm** |\n45\t| **Grace** | No penalty | until **Wed Oct 21, 2026, 2:40 pm** |\n46\t\n47\tAround the exercises you pick, two short parts are required and worth 0 points: Part 0, before you start (15 minutes), and Part 2, submit (20 minutes).\n48\t\n49\t### Prerequisites\n50\t- **Your MP2 repo**, `iphs400-mp2-cms`, with `mp2-final` pushed. The MP2 resubmission is due Thu Oct 15, 2:40 pm (no-penalty grace until Fri Oct 16, 2:40 pm); Part 0 says how the two overlap.\n51\t- **Your MP2 setup still working:** `uv`, `gh` logged in, Claude Code with the mattpocock skills (`/implement`, `/tdd`, `/code-review`, `/prototype`, `/handoff`), the hooks, and the usage ledger.\n52\t- **These two files on GitHub.** Your repo was copied before they existed. Read them in the starter repo, `jon-chun/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter`: this manual and `docs/mp2plus-grading-rubric_20261012.md`.\n53\t\n54\t> **Policy (set by the instructor).** MP2plus was assigned **Sun Oct 11, 2026**, after the first MP2 final submissions were graded, to give deeper hands-on practice and a way to close the gaps the MP2 rubric found. It is an optional menu of **15 independent exercises**. Each takes **15–60 minutes** and is worth **5–10 points** according to its time and difficulty: about 1 point per 6 minutes.\n55\t> **Points are added to the student's MP2 grade**, for every student, whatever the MP2 score. MP2 is graded as a numeric score out of 100. MP2plus points are added after the MP2 resubmission (due Thu Oct 15, 2026, 2:40 pm; no-penalty grace until Fri Oct 16, 2:40 pm) is graded. **Cap: +30 per student.** The sum may exceed 100 and is recorded as is: MP2 91 + MP2plus 24 = 115.\n56\t> **Due Tue Oct 20, 2026, 2:40 pm**; no-penalty grace until **Wed Oct 21, 2026, 2:40 pm**. One MP2plus resubmission within one week of feedback.\n57\t> **The gate.** An exercise earns points only if, at `mp2plus-final`, the MP2 checker (`check_submission.py --stage 2`) and `uv run pytest -q` show no failure that was absent at `mp2plus-base`. A failing test added for MP2plus costs only its own exercise's Tests point. Failures already present at `mp2plus-base` are reported, not scored, so MP2plus is not a repair pass. Solo work: every commit after `mp2plus-base` is authored by the student. No `mp2plus-base` tag, no points.\n58\t\n59\t### Deliverables checklist\n60\tTick every line that applies before you tag `mp2plus-final`.\n61\t\n62\t- [ ] Tag `mp2plus-base` pushed before your first MP2plus commit\n63\t- [ ] `notes/mp2plus-plan.md` committed: the exercises you intend, minute estimates, the base check results\n64\t- [ ] Each exercise you did: everything its **Deliverables** line names\n65\t- [ ] `docs/iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_report_{first}-{last}_{YYYYMMDD}.md` with each exercise's **Report row**, committed before the tag\n66\t- [ ] No checker or test failure that was not there at `mp2plus-base`; tag `mp2plus-final` pushed; email sent\n67\t\n68\t---\n69\t\n70\t## Part 0 — Before you start\n71\t**Time: 15 min. No points, but required: without `mp2plus-base`, no exercise earns points.**\n72\t\n73\t### 0.1 Tag your baseline\n74\t`mp2plus-base` marks the commit graded for MP2. Everything after it is MP2plus, and the judge scores only that range. Run the two MP2 checks first:\n75\t\n76\t```bash\n77\tcd ~/code/iphs400-mp2-cms\n78\tgit switch main && git pull\n79\tuv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2\n80\tuv run pytest -q\n81\t```\n82\t\n83\t**Expected:** the checker ends with `N/N checks passed.` and pytest ends with `passed`. A `FAIL` line or a failing test here is a pre-existing failure. Copy it into your plan (0.2). It is reported, not scored, and you need not fix it for MP2plus. Then tag the commit graded for MP2:\n84\t\n85\t```bash\n86\tgit tag mp2plus-base mp2-final\n87\tgit push origin mp2plus-base\n88\t```\n89\t\n90\t**Expected:** `* [new tag] mp2plus-base -> mp2plus-base`.\n91\t\n92\t- **Resubmitting MP2 by Oct 15?** The simplest order is to push your revised `mp2-final` first, then run the two commands above.\n93\t- **Starting MP2plus before you resubmit?** Tag now. Make the MP2 fixes on a branch from `mp2-final` (`git switch -c mp2-resubmit mp2-final`), move the tag there (`git tag -f mp2-final && git push -f origin mp2-final`), and `git switch main` to continue MP2plus. Before you tag `mp2plus-final`, run `git merge mp2-resubmit` on `main` and name the merge commit in your report. Those commits are MP2 work, and MP2plus does not score them.\n94\t\n95\t### 0.2 Write your plan\n96\tSkim the menu and list what you intend to do, with minute estimates from the menu. The plan may change; your report says what you actually did. Create `notes/mp2plus-plan.md`, then commit it on `main` with the message `mp2plus: plan` and push:\n97\t\n98\t```text\n99\t# MP2plus plan\n100\tExercises: F2 about 50 min; S2 about 50 min; P4 about 35 min\n101\tAt mp2plus-base: checker \"<its last line>\", FAIL lines: <names, or none>; pytest \"<its last line>\"\n102\t```\n103\t\n104\tIf you picked P4, its \"before\" run goes into this file now (see P4).\n105\t\n106\t> **The gate.** At `mp2plus-final` the judge runs the same two checks. A check or a test that passed at `mp2plus-base` and fails at `mp2plus-final` sets every exercise to 0 until a resubmission fixes it. Test files that existed at `mp2plus-base` may change only by adding cases. If an exercise truly needs an existing assertion changed, say so in that exercise's findings comment and its report row; the judge then reviews `git diff mp2plus-base..mp2plus-final` for those files.\n107\t\n108\t---\n109\t\n110\t## Part 1 — The menu\n111\t- **Pick any.** The exercises are independent. P1 carries one other change, P2 needs code where its decision lands, and P4 measures one other exercise; each says so under **Prerequisites**.\n112\t- **New work only.** Only commits after `mp2plus-base` count. A feature already in your repo at `mp2plus-base` is not scored again.\n113\t- **Every point is a line** with a measure and a check, listed under each exercise's **Scoring**. One flaw costs points in one line only.\n114\t\n115\t**How each exercise is laid out.** Every exercise has the same headings: Goal, Prerequisites, Roles, Steps, Prompt, Acceptance checklist, Out of scope, Deliverables, Report row, Scoring, If it goes wrong. The **Roles** line says which new routes are admin-only and which editors may use; S1 tests exactly those. The **Acceptance checklist** is the contract: the judge checks those steps and no others. Its **Checked by** column uses seven words. *walk*: the judge clicks through your app from a clean clone, at 1280 and 390 px. *publish*: the judge runs `uv run cms publish` and inspects `site/`. *test*: a named test for this step exists and passes. *read*: the judge reads the file or the code. *replay*: the judge sends the form's POST again without its CSRF token. *github*: the judge reads GitHub's own records and times (issues, pull requests, comments, pushes). *run*: the judge runs the command at the commit named.\n116\t\n117\t> **How a feature scores.** A feature worth P points has four lines. **Screenshots, 1:** both `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-{slug}-1280.png` and `-390.png` are present. **Trail, 1:** the issue existed before your first commit for it reached GitHub, and your findings comment came before the issue closed. **Tests, 1:** every step marked *test* has a named test that passes. **Function, P − 3:** floor((P − 3) × steps passed ÷ steps in the table). Process and security exercises score one point per checklist row, as listed in their tables.\n118\t\n119\t### The feature runbook\n120\tEvery feature's **Steps** follow MP2 Part 6's per-ticket loop. The commands, once:\n121\t\n122\t1. **The issue, before any code.** `gh issue create --label stretch --title \"MP2plus F2: Categories and tags\"`. When `gh` asks for the body, open the editor and paste the feature's acceptance table (the `| # | Step | Checked by |` rows) word for word, then a last line `Blocked by: none`. If `gh` says the label is not found, run `gh label create stretch` once and retry.\n123\t2. **The phase, before the session.** `echo T14 > .claude/state/phase`, with your issue number for 14. The usage ledger labels every turn with it, so set it before you start. Process and security exercises set their id instead, for example `echo S2 > .claude/state/phase`.\n124\t3. **The build.** `/clear`, then the feature's prompt with your issue number. `/implement` drives `/tdd`: a failing test first, then code.\n125\t4. **Your own walk.** Click through the acceptance checklist at 1280 and 390 px; fix what fails.\n126\t5. **Review, then close.** Send `/code-review`, then: `Post the code-review findings and how each was resolved as a comment on issue #14, then commit and push with a message that starts \"T14:\" and ends \"Closes #14\".`\n127\t6. **Check.** `gh issue view 14`. **Expected:** state CLOSED, with your findings comment above the close.\n128\t7. **Screenshots.** The feature working, at 1280 and 390 px, saved as named in its **Deliverables**.\n129\t8. **The two checks.** `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` and `uv run pytest -q`. Fix any failure that was not there at `mp2plus-base` before you start the next exercise.\n130\t\n131\tEvery feature prompt ends with the same rules; each one guards against a way to lose points. No `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` in any template, admin pages included: the MP2 checker greps every tracked `.html` file. A schema change needs a fresh database: `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`. A new setting needs a line in `.env.example`, because the judge starts your app from it. Every new form needs a CSRF token.\n132\t\n133\t| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n134\t|---|---|---|\n135\t| Checker fails `no root-absolute paths in HTML` after a new admin page | a template has `href=\"/admin/...\"` | use `url_for(...)` or a relative link; the checker reads admin templates too |\n136\t| `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column` | the schema changed; your old `cms.db` did not | `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` |\n137\t| An MP2 test fails after your change | the feature changed behaviour an old test pins | add cases, never weaken old ones; if one assertion truly must change, declare it (Part 0 gate box) |\n138\t| Issue did not close | the commit message or PR body lacked `Closes #N` | `gh issue close 14 --comment \"closed by <sha>\"`; use the exact phrase next time |\n139\t| Checker fails on a transcript name | a file in `docs/transcripts/` breaks MP2's pattern | set `CMS_STUDENT=first-last` in `.env`; rename to `iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_{NN}_{first}-{last}_{YYYYMMDD}.md` |\n140\t| Your exercise has no row in `usage_report.py` | the phase was set after the session started | set it first next time; the ledger cannot be relabelled |\n141\t### 1.1 Features (F1–F9)\n142\t\n143\t#### F1 Media uploads with alt text (9 pts, about 45–60 min)\n144\t- **Goal.** Editors upload images to a media library and place them in posts. Every image carries alt text, so a screen reader can describe it.\n145\t- **Prerequisites.** MP2 done and Part 0 complete. Other exercises: none. Uses FastAPI's form uploads (`python-multipart` is already a dependency).\n146\t- **Roles.** Upload and media library: admin and editor.\n147\t\n148\t**Steps.**\n149\t1. Create the issue (runbook 1), title `MP2plus F1: Media uploads with alt text`; then `echo T<issue#> > .claude/state/phase`.\n150\t2. `/clear`, then the prompt below with your issue number. Then walk the acceptance checklist yourself; fix what fails.\n151\t3. `/code-review`, then the close-out message (runbook 5). `gh issue view <issue#>` shows CLOSED, with your comment above the close.\n152\t4. Save `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `mp2plus-media-390.png`: the library with one image. Then run the two checks (runbook 8).\n153\t\n154\t**Prompt.**\n155\t```text\n156\t/implement #N Media uploads with alt text, for posts only. Follow the issue's acceptance checklist exactly. Store uploads under media/ and add media/ to .gitignore. Accept PNG and JPEG of 2 MB or less; check the type by extension and by the file's first bytes. The library shows a copyable Markdown snippet ![alt](media/<file>) for each item. cms publish copies media/ into site/media/ and makes every image src relative to the page that contains it. Rules: no href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template, admin pages included; use url_for or relative links. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses a POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. If you change the database schema, keep scripts/seed_demo.py running clean from .env.example and tell me to run rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py. Tests that existed before may only gain cases; ask me before changing an existing assertion. Put the new tests in tests/test_media.py and name each one test_step<k>_<what> after the acceptance step it checks. Ask before adding any dependency.\n157\t```\n158\t**Acceptance checklist.**\n159\t| # | Step | Checked by |\n160\t|---|---|---|\n161\t| 1 | Upload a PNG or JPEG of 2 MB or less with alt text; it appears in the media library | walk, test |\n162\t| 2 | An upload with empty alt text is refused with a message | walk, test |\n163\t| 3 | A `.html` file, a `.html` file renamed to `.png`, and any file over 2 MB are refused: the type is checked by extension and by the file's first bytes | walk, test |\n164\t| 4 | Uploads are stored under `media/`, and `media/` is git-ignored | read |\n165\t| 5 | Each library item shows a copyable Markdown snippet, `![<alt text>](media/<file>)` | walk |\n166\t| 6 | The upload form carries a CSRF token; its POST replayed without the token is refused | replay, test |\n167\t| 7 | After `uv run cms publish`, the file is in `site/media/`, and the post's `<img>` has the alt text and a relative `src` that loads in the preview | publish, test |\n168\t\n169\t**The judge runs:** upload an image; try an empty alt text, a `.html` file and a `.html` file renamed to `.png`; paste a snippet into a published post; publish; preview with `python3 -m http.server -d site 8001`; check that every `<img>` in `site/` has `alt=` and loads.\n170\t- **Out of scope.** Inserting images with a button, resizing, thumbnails, deleting media, video, drag-and-drop, images in pages.\n171\t- **Deliverables.** The closed issue; `tests/test_media.py`; `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `-390.png`; your report row.\n172\t- **Report row.** `| F1 | issue #<n>; tests/test_media.py; mp2plus-media-1280.png, mp2plus-media-390.png |`\n173\t- **Scoring.** Screenshots 1 · Trail 1 · Tests 1 · Function 6 = floor(6 × steps passed ÷ 7). Total 9.\n174\t\n175\t**If it goes wrong.**\n176\t| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n177\t|---|---|---|\n178\t| Images load on the home page, broken on post pages | a post page needs `../media/x.png` | make `src` relative to each page's folder |\n179\t| A renamed `.html` file is accepted | only the extension is checked | compare the first bytes with the PNG and JPEG signatures |\n180\t#### F2 Categories and tags (8 pts, about 40–55 min)\n181\t- **Goal.** Readers browse by topic. Each post has one category and any number of tags, and the public site has one index page per category and per tag.\n182\t- **Prerequisites.** MP2 done and Part 0 complete. Other exercises: none. A schema change: rebuild `cms.db` afterwards.\n183\t- **Roles.** Category and tag fields in the post editor, and the category filter: admin and editor.\n184\t\n185\t**Steps.**\n186\t1. Create the issue (runbook 1), title `MP2plus F2: Categories and tags`; then `echo T<issue#> > .claude/state/phase`.\n187\t2. `/clear`, then the prompt below with your issue number. Then `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`, then walk the acceptance checklist yourself; fix what fails.\n188\t3. `/code-review`, then the close-out message (runbook 5). `gh issue view <issue#>` shows CLOSED, with your comment above the close.\n189\t4. Save `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-categories-1280.png` and `mp2plus-categories-390.png`: a published category page. Then run the two checks (runbook 8).\n190\t\n191\t**Prompt.**\n192\t```text\n193\t/implement #N Categories and tags, for posts only. Follow the issue's acceptance checklist exactly. One category per post as a single field; tags as one comma-separated field. The admin content list filters by category only. cms publish writes site/category/<slug>.html and site/tag/<slug>.html with published posts only, and every link between them is relative. Add the new terms to CONTEXT.md. Rules: no href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template, admin pages included; use url_for or relative links. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses a POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. If you change the database schema, keep scripts/seed_demo.py running clean from .env.example and tell me to run rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py. Tests that existed before may only gain cases; ask me before changing an existing assertion. Put the new tests in tests/test_taxonomy.py and name each one test_step<k>_<what> after the acceptance step it checks. Ask before adding any dependency.\n194\t```\n195\t**Acceptance checklist.**\n196\t| # | Step | Checked by |\n197\t|---|---|---|\n198\t| 1 | A post has one category (a single field) and tags (one comma-separated field); both persist after save | walk, test |\n199\t| 2 | The admin content list filters by category | walk, test |\n200\t| 3 | `uv run cms publish` writes `site/category/<slug>.html` and `site/tag/<slug>.html`, each listing its published posts | publish, test |\n201\t| 4 | Each published post links to its category page and its tag pages with relative paths | publish |\n202\t| 5 | A draft with the same category and tag is absent from both index pages | publish, test |\n203\t\n204\t**The judge runs:** give two posts a category and tags; filter the admin list by category; publish; open a category page and a tag page from a post's links; add a draft with the same category and tag, publish again, and check it is absent.\n205\t- **Out of scope.** Nested categories, tag clouds, a tag filter in the admin list, categories on pages, renaming a tag across posts.\n206\t- **Deliverables.** The closed issue; `tests/test_taxonomy.py`; `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-categories-1280.png` and `-390.png`; your report row.\n207\t- **Report row.** `| F2 | issue #<n>; tests/test_taxonomy.py; mp2plus-categories-1280.png, mp2plus-categories-390.png |`\n208\t- **Scoring.** Screenshots 1 · Trail 1 · Tests 1 · Function 5 = floor(5 × steps passed ÷ 5). Total 8.\n209\t\n210\t**If it goes wrong.**\n211\t| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n212\t|---|---|---|\n213\t| Category links break from a post page | a post page needs `../category/x.html` | make links relative to each page's folder |\n214\t| A tag with a space makes a broken file name | no slug was generated | slugify tag and category names for file names |\n215\t#### F3 Revision history with rollback (8 pts, about 40–55 min)\n216\t- **Goal.** Nobody loses work to a bad edit. Every save of a post stores a revision, and rolling back copies an old revision forward as a new one, so the history only grows.\n217\t- **Prerequisites.** MP2 done and Part 0 complete. Other exercises: none. A schema change: rebuild `cms.db` afterwards.\n218\t- **Roles.** Revision list, revision view and rollback: admin and editor.\n219\t\n220\t**Steps.**\n221\t1. Create the issue (runbook 1), title `MP2plus F3: Revision history with rollback`; then `echo T<issue#> > .claude/state/phase`.\n222\t2. `/clear`, then the prompt below with your issue number. Then `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`, then walk the acceptance checklist yourself; fix what fails.\n223\t3. `/code-review`, then the close-out message (runbook 5). `gh issue view <issue#>` shows CLOSED, with your comment above the close.\n224\t4. Save `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-revisions-1280.png` and `mp2plus-revisions-390.png`: a post's revision list. Then run the two checks (runbook 8).\n225\t\n226\t**Prompt.**\n227\t```text\n228\t/implement #N Revision history with rollback, for posts only. Follow the issue's acceptance checklist exactly. Store revisions in their own table, with who, when, title and body, written on every save including the first create. Rollback is a POST that creates a new revision; it never deletes or rewrites an old one. Rules: no href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template, admin pages included; use url_for or relative links. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses a POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. If you change the database schema, keep scripts/seed_demo.py running clean from .env.example and tell me to run rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py. Tests that existed before may only gain cases; ask me before changing an existing assertion. Put the new tests in tests/test_revisions.py and name each one test_step<k>_<what> after the acceptance step it checks. Ask before adding any dependency.\n229\t```\n230\t**Acceptance checklist.**\n231\t| # | Step | Checked by |\n232\t|---|---|---|\n233\t| 1 | Every save of a post, the first create included, stores a revision with who, when, title and body | test |\n234\t| 2 | The admin lists a post's revisions, newest first, and shows any one of them | walk |\n235\t| 3 | Creating a post and saving it twice more lists three revisions | walk, test |\n236\t| 4 | Rolling back to revision 1 adds revision 4, whose title and body equal revision 1's; nothing is deleted | walk, test |\n237\t| 5 | The rollback form carries a CSRF token; its POST replayed without the token is refused | replay, test |\n238\t| 6 | Revisions survive a server restart | walk |\n239\t\n240\t**The judge runs:** create a post and save it twice more (three revisions); roll back to revision 1 (four revisions, revision 1's body); replay the rollback POST without its token; restart the server and check the list again.\n241\t- **Out of scope.** Revisions of pages, users or settings; side-by-side diffs; pruning; autosave.\n242\t- **Deliverables.** The closed issue; `tests/test_revisions.py`; `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-revisions-1280.png` and `-390.png`; your report row.\n243\t- **Report row.** `| F3 | issue #<n>; tests/test_revisions.py; mp2plus-revisions-1280.png, mp2plus-revisions-390.png |`\n244\t- **Scoring.** Screenshots 1 · Trail 1 · Tests 1 · Function 5 = floor(5 × steps passed ÷ 6). Total 8.\n245\t\n246\t**If it goes wrong.**\n247\t| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n248\t|---|---|---|\n249\t| Two revisions per save | both the create and the update path write one | write the revision in one shared save function |\n250\t| Rollback is a link, not a form | a GET changes state | make it a POST form with a CSRF token |\n251\t#### F4 Scheduled publishing (7 pts, about 35–50 min)\n252\t- **Goal.** An author finishes a post on Sunday and wants it public on Tuesday. The post gets a `publish_at` time and the status `scheduled`, and goes public the next time you publish after that time.\n253\t- **Prerequisites.** MP2 done and Part 0 complete. Other exercises: none. A new setting, `CMS_TIMEZONE` (default `America/New_York`), read with Python's `zoneinfo`; a schema change.\n254\t- **Roles.** Scheduling in the post editor: admin and editor.\n255\t\n256\t**Steps.**\n257\t1. Create the issue (runbook 1), title `MP2plus F4: Scheduled publishing`; then `echo T<issue#> > .claude/state/phase`.\n258\t2. `/clear`, then the prompt below with your issue number. Then `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`, then walk the acceptance checklist yourself; fix what fails.\n259\t3. `/code-review`, then the close-out message (runbook 5). `gh issue view <issue#>` shows CLOSED, with your comment above the close.\n260\t4. Save `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-scheduled-1280.png` and `mp2plus-scheduled-390.png`: the admin list with a scheduled post. Then run the two checks (runbook 8).\n261\t\n262\t**Prompt.**\n263\t```text\n264\t/implement #N Scheduled publishing, for posts only. Follow the issue's acceptance checklist exactly. Total 7.\n281\t\n282\t**If it goes wrong.**\n283\t| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n284\t|---|---|---|\n285\t| The test passes today, fails tomorrow | the code reads the real clock | pass `now` into the filter; tests pass a fixed time |\n286\t| A post goes public hours early or late | naive times compared with UTC | store aware times; compare in `CMS_TIMEZONE` |\n287\t#### F5 Site search (7 pts, about 35–50 min)\n288\t- **Goal.** Readers find a post without scrolling. `cms publish` writes a small search index and a `search.html` page that queries it with one short script. Add CMS_ENV=development and CMS_ADMIN_EMAIL to .env.example and a Production section to README.md. Development behaviour does not change. Rules: no href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template, admin pages included; use url_for or relative links. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses a POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. Total 8.\n460\t\n461\t**If it goes wrong.**\n462\t| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n463\t|---|---|---|\n464\t| Tests pass alone, fail together | a test changed `os.environ` | pass a dict to the check function; never set the real environment |\n465\t| Production mode starts with the `.env` secret | `.env` overrides the command line | load `.env` without overriding variables already set |\n466\t### 1.2 Process (P1–P4)\n467\t\n468\t#### P1 Pull-request workflow (6 pts, about 30–45 min)\n469\t- **Goal.** Ship one change through a branch, a pull request and a review before the merge, the way most teams work.\n470\t- **Prerequisites.** Part 0 complete. P1 carries one change: a feature from this menu (scored as that feature too), or one item from your MP2 feedback's repair list, written as a small issue. A repair earns P1's points only, not MP2 points.\n471\t- **Roles.** No new routes of its own; a carried feature keeps its own Roles line.\n472\t\n473\t**Steps.**\n474\t1. Create the issue first. For a feature, that feature's step 1. For a repair: `gh issue create --label stretch --title \"MP2plus P1: <the repair>\"`, body = two to four acceptance steps, then `Blocked by: none`. Set the phase: `echo T<issue#> > .claude/state/phase` for a feature, `echo P1 > .claude/state/phase` for a repair.\n475\t2. Branch: `git switch main && git pull && git switch -c mp2plus-<slug>`.\n476\t3. `/clear`, then the feature's prompt or the prompt below; let it commit on the branch.\n477\t4. `git push -u origin mp2plus-<slug>`, then `gh pr create --title \"MP2plus P1: <the change>\" --body \"Closes #<issue#>\"`.\n478\t5. `/code-review`, then: `Post the code-review findings and how each was resolved as a comment on pull request #<pr#>, then commit and push the fixes to this branch.`\n479\t6. `gh pr merge <pr#> --merge --delete-branch`, then `git switch main && git pull` and `gh issue view <issue#>`. **Expected:** CLOSED, closed by your pull request, with the review comment on the PR dated before the merge.\n480\t\n481\t**Prompt.** For a repair (a feature uses its own prompt):\n482\t```text\n483\t/implement #N <the repair, in one sentence>. Follow the issue's acceptance steps exactly. Rules: no href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template, admin pages included; use url_for or relative links. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses a POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. A menu of optional exercises: pick any, in any order, at your own pace.\n\n---\n\n## Front matter\n### What this is\nMP2plus is a **menu of 15 independent exercises** that extend the CMS you built in MP2. Pick any number, in any order, and stop whenever you like. Your points are **added to your MP2 score**, up to **+30**.\n\nThe menu has three groups:\n- **Features** (F1–F9) come from MP2's stretch list, which MP2 introduced but did not score.\n- **Process** (P1–P4) covers habits MP2 introduced but did not require, or scored only lightly.\n- **Security** (S1–S2) extends two lines of `SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md` that MP2 scored only lightly.\n\n### The menu\n| Id | Exercise | Minutes | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| F1 | Media uploads with alt text | 45–60 | 9 |\n| F2 | Categories and tags | 40–55 | 8 |\n| F3 | Revision history with rollback | 40–55 | 8 |\n| F4 | Scheduled publishing | 35–50 | 7 |\n| F5 | Site search | 35–50 | 7 |\n| F6 | Comments with moderation | 45–60 | 9 |\n| F7 | Plugin or hook system | 45–60 | 9 |\n| F8 | Switchable theme | 35–50 | 7 |\n| F9 | Production configuration | 40–55 | 8 |\n| P1 | Pull-request workflow | 30–45 | 6 |\n| P2 | `/prototype` side session | 35–50 | 7 |\n| P3 | Decision record | 30–45 | 6 |\n| P4 | Budget re-forecast | 30–40 | 6 |\n| S1 | Direct-URL access matrix | 30–45 | 6 |\n| S2 | Login hardening | 40–55 | 8 |\n| | **Menu total (up to 30 count)** | | **111** |\n\nPick what interests you, not everything. No `mp2plus-base` tag, no points.\n\n### Deliverables checklist\nTick every line that applies before you tag `mp2plus-final`.\n\n- [ ] Tag `mp2plus-base` pushed before your first MP2plus commit\n- [ ] `notes/mp2plus-plan.md` committed: the exercises you intend, minute estimates, the base check results\n- [ ] Each exercise you did: everything its **Deliverables** line names\n- [ ] `docs/iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_report_{first}-{last}_{YYYYMMDD}.md` with each exercise's **Report row**, committed before the tag\n- [ ] No checker or test failure that was not there at `mp2plus-base`; tag `mp2plus-final` pushed; email sent\n\n---\n\n## Part 0 — Before you start\n**Time: 15 min. No points, but required: without `mp2plus-base`, no exercise earns points.**\n\n### 0.1 Tag your baseline\n`mp2plus-base` marks the commit graded for MP2. Everything after it is MP2plus, and the judge scores only that range. Run the two MP2 checks first:\n\n```bash\ncd ~/code/iphs400-mp2-cms\ngit switch main && git pull\nuv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2\nuv run pytest -q\n```\n\n**Expected:** the checker ends with `N/N checks passed.` and pytest ends with `passed`. A `FAIL` line or a failing test here is a pre-existing failure. Copy it into your plan (0.2). It is reported, not scored, and you need not fix it for MP2plus. Then tag the commit graded for MP2:\n\n```bash\ngit tag mp2plus-base mp2-final\ngit push origin mp2plus-base\n```\n\n**Expected:** `* [new tag] mp2plus-base -> mp2plus-base`.\n\n- **Resubmitting MP2 by Oct 15?** The simplest order is to push your revised `mp2-final` first, then run the two commands above.\n- **Starting MP2plus before you resubmit?** Tag now. Make the MP2 fixes on a branch from `mp2-final` (`git switch -c mp2-resubmit mp2-final`), move the tag there (`git tag -f mp2-final && git push -f origin mp2-final`), and `git switch main` to continue MP2plus. Before you tag `mp2plus-final`, run `git merge mp2-resubmit` on `main` and name the merge commit in your report. Those commits are MP2 work, and MP2plus does not score them.\n\n### 0.2 Write your plan\nSkim the menu and list what you intend to do, with minute estimates from the menu. The plan may change; your report says what you actually did. Create `notes/mp2plus-plan.md`, then commit it on `main` with the message `mp2plus: plan` and push:\n\n```text\n# MP2plus plan\nExercises: F2 about 50 min; S2 about 50 min; P4 about 35 min\nAt mp2plus-base: checker \"<its last line>\", FAIL lines: <names, or none>; pytest \"<its last line>\"\n```\n\nIf you picked P4, its \"before\" run goes into this file now (see P4).\n\n> **The gate.** At `mp2plus-final` the judge runs the same two checks. If an exercise truly needs an existing assertion changed, say so in that exercise's findings comment and its report row; the judge then reviews `git diff mp2plus-base..mp2plus-final` for those files.\n\n---\n\n## Part 1 — The menu\n- **Pick any.** The exercises are independent. P1 carries one other change, P2 needs code where its decision lands, and P4 measures one other exercise; each says so under **Prerequisites**.\n- **New work only.** Only commits after `mp2plus-base` count. A feature already in your repo at `mp2plus-base` is not scored again.\n- **Every point is a line** with a measure and a check, listed under each exercise's **Scoring**. One flaw costs points in one line only.\n\n**How each exercise is laid out.** Every exercise has the same headings: Goal, Prerequisites, Roles, Steps, Prompt, Acceptance checklist, Out of scope, Deliverables, Report row, Scoring, If it goes wrong. The **Roles** line says which new routes are admin-only and which editors may use; S1 tests exactly those. The **Acceptance checklist** is the contract: the judge checks those steps and no others. Its **Checked by** column uses seven words. *walk*: the judge clicks through your app from a clean clone, at 1280 and 390 px. *publish*: the judge runs `uv run cms publish` and inspects `site/`. *test*: a named test for this step exists and passes. *read*: the judge reads the file or the code. *replay*: the judge sends the form's POST again without its CSRF token. *github*: the judge reads GitHub's own records and times (issues, pull requests, comments, pushes). *run*: the judge runs the command at the commit named.\n\n> **How a feature scores.** A feature worth P points has four lines. **Screenshots, 1:** both `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-{slug}-1280.png` and `-390.png` are present. **Trail, 1:** the issue existed before your first commit for it reached GitHub, and your findings comment came before the issue closed. **Tests, 1:** every step marked *test* has a named test that passes. **Function, P − 3:** floor((P − 3) × steps passed ÷ steps in the table). Process and security exercises score one point per checklist row, as listed in their tables.\n\n### The feature runbook\nEvery feature's **Steps** follow MP2 Part 6's per-ticket loop. The commands, once:\n\n1. **The issue, before any code.** `gh issue create --label stretch --title \"MP2plus F2: Categories and tags\"`. When `gh` asks for the body, open the editor and paste the feature's acceptance table (the `| # | Step | Checked by |` rows) word for word, then a last line `Blocked by: none`. If `gh` says the label is not found, run `gh label create stretch` once and retry.\n2. **The phase, before the session.** `echo T14 > .claude/state/phase`, with your issue number for 14. The usage ledger labels every turn with it, so set it before you start. Process and security exercises set their id instead, for example `echo S2 > .claude/state/phase`.\n3. **The build.** `/clear`, then the feature's prompt with your issue number. `/implement` drives `/tdd`: a failing test first, then code.\n4. **Your own walk.** Click through the acceptance checklist at 1280 and 390 px; fix what fails.\n5. **Review, then close.** Send `/code-review`, then: `Post the code-review findings and how each was resolved as a comment on issue #14, then commit and push with a message that starts \"T14:\" and ends \"Closes #14\".`\n6. **Check.** `gh issue view 14`. **Expected:** state CLOSED, with your findings comment above the close.\n7. **Screenshots.** The feature working, at 1280 and 390 px, saved as named in its **Deliverables**.\n8. **The two checks.** `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` and `uv run pytest -q`. Fix any failure that was not there at `mp2plus-base` before you start the next exercise.\n\nEvery feature prompt ends with the same rules; each one guards against a way to lose points. No `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` in any template, admin pages included: the MP2 checker greps every tracked `.html` file. A schema change needs a fresh database: `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`. A new setting needs a line in `.env.example`, because the judge starts your app from it. Every new form needs a CSRF token.\n\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| Checker fails `no root-absolute paths in HTML` after a new admin page | a template has `href=\"/admin/...\"` | use `url_for(...)` or a relative link; the checker reads admin templates too |\n| `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column` | the schema changed; your old `cms.db` did not | `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` |\n| An MP2 test fails after your change | the feature changed behaviour an old test pins | add cases, never weaken old ones; if one assertion truly must change, declare it (Part 0 gate box) |\n| Issue did not close | the commit message or PR body lacked `Closes #N` | `gh issue close 14 --comment \"closed by <sha>\"`; use the exact phrase next time |\n| Checker fails on a transcript name | a file in `docs/transcripts/` breaks MP2's pattern | set `CMS_STUDENT=first-last` in `.env`; rename to `iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_{NN}_{first}-{last}_{YYYYMMDD}.md` |\n| Your exercise has no row in `usage_report.py` | the phase was set after the session started | set it first next time; the ledger cannot be relabelled |\n### 1.1 Features (F1–F9)\n\n#### F1 Media uploads with alt text (9 pts, about 45–60 min)\n- **Goal.** Editors upload images to a media library and place them in posts. Every image carries alt text, so a screen reader can describe it.\n- **Prerequisites.** MP2 done and Part 0 complete. Other exercises: none. Then run the two checks (runbook 8).\n\n**Prompt.**\n```text\n/implement #N Media uploads with alt text, for posts only. Follow the issue's acceptance checklist exactly. Store uploads under media/ and add media/ to .gitignore. Accept PNG and JPEG of 2 MB or less; check the type by extension and by the file's first bytes. The library shows a copyable Markdown snippet ![alt](media/<file>) for each item. cms publish copies media/ into site/media/ and makes every image src relative to the page that contains it. Ask before adding any dependency.\n```\n**Acceptance checklist.**\n| # | Step | Checked by |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | With `CMS_ENV=production`, `uv run cms serve` refuses to start when `CMS_SECRET_KEY` is unset, equals the development default in `app/settings.py`, or equals the `.env.example` value; the message names the variable | walk, test |\n| 2 | With `CMS_ENV=production`, it also refuses to start when `CMS_ADMIN_EMAIL` or `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is unset, or the password equals the `.env.example` value | test |\n| 3 | With `CMS_ENV=production`, `scripts/seed_demo.py` exits non-zero with a message and creates nothing | walk, test |\n| 4 | Started in production on an empty database, the app creates one admin from `CMS_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`; that login works, and the demo logins from `tests/conftest.py` are refused | walk, test |\n| 5 | `.env.example` lists `CMS_ENV=development` and `CMS_ADMIN_EMAIL`, and the README has a *Production* section naming every variable production needs and the start command | read |\n\n**The judge runs:** `CMS_ENV=production uv run cms serve --port 8001` with the `.env.example` values (refused); the same with fresh values for `CMS_SECRET_KEY`, `CMS_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_DATABASE=prod-check.db` (starts); logs in as that admin and tries the demo logins; runs the seed script with `CMS_ENV=production`.\n- **Out of scope.** Hosting, HTTPS, a live URL, a rate limiter (S2 covers it), email.\n- **Deliverables.** The closed issue; `tests/test_production.py`; `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-production-1280.png` and `-390.png`; the README *Production* section; your report row.\n- **Report row.** `| F9 | issue #<n>; tests/test_production.py; mp2plus-production-1280.png, mp2plus-production-390.png |`\n- **Scoring.** Screenshots 1 · Trail 1 · Tests 1 · Function 5 = floor(5 × steps passed ÷ 5). Total 8.\n\n**If it goes wrong.**\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| Tests pass alone, fail together | a test changed `os.environ` | pass a dict to the check function; never set the real environment |\n| Production mode starts with the `.env` secret | `.env` overrides the command line | load `.env` without overriding variables already set |\n### 1.2 Process (P1–P4)\n\n#### P1 Pull-request workflow (6 pts, about 30–45 min)\n- **Goal.** Ship one change through a branch, a pull request and a review before the merge, the way most teams work.\n- **Prerequisites.** Part 0 complete. P1 carries one change: a feature from this menu (scored as that feature too), or one item from your MP2 feedback's repair list, written as a small issue. A repair earns P1's points only, not MP2 points.\n- **Roles.** No new routes of its own; a carried feature keeps its own Roles line.\n\n**Steps.**\n1. Create the issue first. For a feature, that feature's step 1. For a repair: `gh issue create --label stretch --title \"MP2plus P1: <the repair>\"`, body = two to four acceptance steps, then `Blocked by: none`. Set the phase: `echo T<issue#> > .claude/state/phase` for a feature, `echo P1 > .claude/state/phase` for a repair.\n2. Branch: `git switch main && git pull && git switch -c mp2plus-<slug>`.\n3. `/clear`, then the feature's prompt or the prompt below; let it commit on the branch.\n4. `git push -u origin mp2plus-<slug>`, then `gh pr create --title \"MP2plus P1: <the change>\" --body \"Closes #<issue#>\"`.\n5. `/code-review`, then: `Post the code-review findings and how each was resolved as a comment on pull request #<pr#>, then commit and push the fixes to this branch.`\n6. `gh pr merge <pr#> --merge --delete-branch`, then `git switch main && git pull` and `gh issue view <issue#>`. **Expected:** CLOSED, closed by your pull request, with the review comment on the PR dated before the merge.\n\n**Prompt.** For a repair (a feature uses its own prompt):\n```text\n/implement #N <the repair, in one sentence>. Follow the issue's acceptance steps exactly. Rules: no href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template, admin pages included; use url_for or relative links. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses a POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. If you change the database schema, keep scripts/seed_demo.py running clean from .env.example and tell me to run rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py. Tests that existed before may only gain cases; ask me before changing an existing assertion. Ask before adding any dependency.\n```\n**Acceptance checklist.**\n| # | Step | Checked by | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | The issue's `createdAt` is before the branch's first push | github | 1 |\n| 2 | The PR comes from a branch off `main`, and its body contains `Closes #<issue#>` | github | 1 |\n| 3 | A `/code-review` findings comment on the PR, listing each finding and how it was resolved, is dated before `mergedAt` | github | 2 |\n| 4 | At least one commit was pushed to the branch after that comment | github | 1 |\n| 5 | The PR is merged, and the merge closed the issue | github | 1 |\n\n- **Out of scope.** Reviews by another person, protected branches, CI.\n- **Deliverables.** The closed issue; the merged PR; your report row.\n- **Report row.** `| P1 | PR #<n> closing issue #<n>; carries <F-id, or \"MP2 repair: <what>\"> |`\n- **Scoring.** One point per row as listed. Total 6. When P1 carries a feature, row 3's comment is also that feature's findings comment (its Trail line); a missing or late comment costs both.\n  - ✅ *\"Findings: (1) upload accepted a renamed `.html` file; fixed by checking the first bytes, test added. (2) suggested Pillow for resizing; rejected, resizing is out of scope.\"* Posted before the merge.\n  - ❌ *\"LGTM\"*, or any comment posted after the merge.\n\n**If it goes wrong.**\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| The PR shows unrelated commits | you branched from another branch | ask Claude to explain a rebase onto `main` before running it |\n| The review found nothing to fix | a small change | ask `/code-review` for the weakest test in the diff and strengthen it; that is your fix commit |\n#### P2 `/prototype` side session (7 pts, about 35–50 min)\n- **Goal.** Settle one design question with throwaway code instead of guessing, then carry the answer back into your real code.\n- **Prerequisites.** Part 0 complete. Code where the decision lands: a feature you build in MP2plus, or a small commit on `main`.\n- **Roles.** No new routes.\n\n**Steps.**\n1. `echo P2 > .claude/state/phase`. Pick a question that fits one of `/prototype`'s two modes. Logic: *\"Can a rejected comment be approved later, and what does the export show?\"* Look: *\"Which of three media-library layouts works at 390 px?\"*\n2. `git switch -c prototype-<topic>`, then `/clear` and `/prototype <your question, in one sentence>`.\n3. When you have an answer, commit the prototype on that branch, `git push -u origin prototype-<topic>`, then `git switch main`. Carry the decision into the code on `main`, and add a `CONTEXT.md` entry naming it.\n4. `/handoff Record this prototype in four parts: the question, what was tried (branch prototype-<topic>), the finding, and what was carried back (the file path on main).`\n5. `/handoff` tells you the path of the file it wrote; copy it to `docs/handoff/{NN}_prototype-{topic}_{YYYYMMDD}.md`, `{NN}` continuing the folder's numbering. Commit with a message that starts `P2:` and push.\n\n**Prompt.** The `/prototype` and `/handoff` lines in steps 2 and 4.\n\n**Acceptance checklist.**\n| # | Step | Checked by | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `docs/handoff/<NN>_prototype-<topic>_<YYYYMMDD>.md` exists, with `<NN>` continuing that folder's numbering | read | 1 |\n| 2 | It states the design question in one sentence | read | 1 |\n| 3 | It says what was tried and names the prototype branch, which exists on GitHub | read, github | 1 |\n| 4 | It states the finding with one concrete observation: a number, a state the model reached, or the variant chosen | read | 1 |\n| 5 | It says what was carried back, with the file path on `main` where the decision lands | read | 1 |\n| 6 | The code at that path implements the decision | read | 1 |\n| 7 | `CONTEXT.md` has an entry naming the decision | read | 1 |\n\n- **Out of scope.** Polishing the prototype, tests for it, merging its branch.\n- **Deliverables.** `docs/handoff/{NN}_prototype-{topic}_{YYYYMMDD}.md`; the pushed `prototype-<topic>` branch; the `CONTEXT.md` entry; your report row.\n- **Report row.** `| P2 | docs/handoff/<file>; branch prototype-<topic>; decision in <file path> |`\n- **Scoring.** One point per row as listed. Total 7.\n\n**If it goes wrong.**\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| Your `/prototype` offers neither mode | a different skill version | ask Claude for a throwaway script on the branch; the handoff parts are the same |\n| You cannot find the handoff file | the skill saves outside the repo | ask `where did you save the handoff?` |\n#### P3 Decision record (6 pts, about 30–45 min)\n- **Goal.** Write down why your CMS is the way it is, so the next developer, or you in a month, does not undo a choice by accident.\n- **Prerequisites.** Part 0 complete. Decisions you made in MP2 or MP2plus, already in the code.\n- **Roles.** No new routes.\n\n**Steps.**\n1. `echo P3 > .claude/state/phase`, then `ls docs/adr/` and take the next free number. The template ships ADR-001 and ADR-002.\n2. Add a **Decisions** table to `CONTEXT.md` with at least three rows: question, choice, why. Write the \"why\" yourself.\n3. `/clear`, then the prompt below for the decision that is hardest to reverse. Edit the draft until it says what you mean.\n4. Commit with a message that starts `P3:` and push.\n\n**Prompt.**\n```text\nWrite docs/adr/ADR-<NNN>-<slug>.md in the format of docs/adr/ADR-002-stack.md. Decision: <what I decided>. Context: <what forced it>. Name the options I rejected and why. Keep it under 30 lines.\n```\n\n- ✅ `| Where do uploads live? | media/ at the repo root, git-ignored | Photos are 1–3 MB each; I did not want them in git history, same reason as cms.db |`\n- ❌ `| Storage | Local filesystem | Simple, efficient, and follows best practices |` (it restates the choice)\n\n**Acceptance checklist.**\n| # | Step | Checked by | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `CONTEXT.md` has a **Decisions** table with at least three rows: question, choice, why | read | 1 |\n| 2 | Row 1's \"why\" gives a real reason in your own words (a client fact, a measurement or a constraint), not a restatement of the choice | read | 1 |\n| 3 | Row 2's \"why\" passes the same test | read | 1 |\n| 4 | Row 3's \"why\" passes the same test | read | 1 |\n| 5 | `docs/adr/ADR-<NNN>-<slug>.md`, numbered with the next free number, records the hardest-to-reverse decision in ADR-002's format (status, date, context, decision, consequences) and names at least one rejected option | read | 1 |\n| 6 | The ADR's decision matches the code | read | 1 |\n\n- **Out of scope.** Rewriting ADR-001 or ADR-002; ADRs for easy-to-reverse choices.\n- **Deliverables.** The Decisions table in `CONTEXT.md`; `docs/adr/ADR-<NNN>-<slug>.md`; your report row.\n- **Report row.** `| P3 | CONTEXT.md Decisions table; docs/adr/ADR-<NNN>-<slug>.md |`\n- **Scoring.** One point per row as listed. Total 6.\n\n**If it goes wrong.**\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| The ADR describes a decision the code does not show | it was planned, not built | pick a decision that is in the code |\n#### P4 Budget re-forecast (6 pts, about 30–40 min)\n- **Goal.** Forecast what your next exercises will cost in usage, then measure what they did cost and explain the gap.","numLines":580,"startLine":1,"totalLines":746,"truncatedByTokenCap":true}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d045f82f-96e3-47b1-930a-61773c2c051c","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"93e7fd77-5141-4f2b-a39d-a171d2f6ba18","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"93e7fd77-5141-4f2b-a39d-a171d2f6ba18","version":"2.1.303","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}
